Community over Code Glasgow 2026 (October 11–14) is over. | Event website | Hackathon retrospective

Apache Doris — Hackathon

Apache Doris is an open-source, real-time database for modern analytics and AI. It answers sub-second queries under high concurrency at petabyte scale; it treats structured, text and vector data as first-class citizens in the same engine, so a single SQL statement can combine a filter, a BM25 text match and a nearest-neighbour search over embeddings; it queries Iceberg, Delta Lake and Hudi tables in place, with no copy, which makes it an acceleration layer over an open lakehouse rather than yet another silo; and increasingly it serves as the store agents run on — columnar JSON for tool-call traces, BM25 retrieval for RAG and agent memory, MCP for access.

Community over Code Glasgow 2026 (October 11–14) is over. | Event website | Hackathon retrospective

Apache Fluss — Hackathon

Fluss is a streaming storage system for real-time analytics. A table is stored as a log, optionally with a key-value index beside it, and older data is tiered into Iceberg, Paimon or Lance so a single query can read both the lake and the fresh log tail. There is a Java client, a Rust client, and Python, C++ and Elixir bindings built on the Rust one.

item.description:
Community over Code 2026 — Glasgow, UK, October 11–14

Community over Code Glasgow 2026 (October 11–14) is over. | Event website | Hackathon retrospective

Apache Superset — Hackathon

Coordinator

  • Evan Rusackas — evan@apache.org

What We’re Working On

We’re focusing on approachable, well-scoped tasks that don’t require deep familiarity with the codebase to get started on:

  • Small bug fixes — GitHub issues labeled “good first issue”, plus other small, self-contained bugs from the open issues list
  • Linting rules — tightening up our oxlint/ruff configuration and fixing the violations that surface once a rule graduates from warning to error
  • Closing stale issues — triaging old issues to confirm whether they’re still reproducible, need more info, or can be closed
  • Reviewing open pull requests — Superset has a large PR backlog; giving PRs a careful read, testing them locally, and leaving useful feedback is just as valuable as writing new code
  • DRY / tidy-up fixes — finding duplicated logic, dead code, or inconsistent patterns across the codebase and cleaning them up
  • Building new extensions — Superset has a growing extensions framework for building new capabilities without forking core; the quick start guide is a good jumping-off point

We are moving fast, so by the time of the hackathon some of the issues we might point at today may be already solved, so we will have a curated list of issues for the hackathon participants close to the date.

Coordinate Your Community Event Here

This site is available to all ASF project communities to organize and promote meetups, hackathons, sprints, release parties, or any community gathering. Whether you’re planning something local or virtual, we can help you get the word out.

To get started:

  1. Read the How to Organize a Small Apache Event guide
  2. Copy one of our event page templates
  3. Submit a PR to this repo with your event page
  4. Send a note to dev@community.apache.org to let us know about your PR – we can help review and publicize

Or, if you’d rather not deal with PRs: just send a note to dev@community.apache.org describing your event and we’ll set up a page for you.

item.title: Glasgow Bars & Pubs
item.description:
Community over Code Glasgow 2026 - October 11-14, Hilton Glasgow

A guide to bars, pubs, and nightlife near the Community over Code Glasgow venue (Hilton Glasgow, 1 William St, city centre).

Glasgow has a legendary pub culture. Here are some highlights within walking distance of the conference venue.

Good Beer Guide Pubs (CAMRA-recommended)

Babbity Bowster

  • What: Tucked-away pub-restaurant-hotel in Merchant City with a reputation for excellent beer, wine, and food. Beer garden.
  • Where: 16-18 Blackfriars Street, Glasgow G1 1PE (map)
  • Good for: Craft beer, quieter conversation, good food

Classic Glasgow Pubs

The Belle

  • What: Mixed-clientele favourite with suits, students, and dogs by an open fire
  • Where: Great Western Road, Glasgow (map)
  • Good for: Cosy atmosphere, good pints, open fire in October

Felson’s

  • What: Pool tables, HD sports screens, burgers and pints
  • Where: City centre, Glasgow (map)
  • Good for: Groups, casual hangouts, watching football

Hope & Vincent

  • What: Pub/lounge bar with pool table, jukebox, and an eight-foot sports screen
  • Where: City centre, Glasgow (map)
  • Good for: Laid-back vibes, entertainment, group gatherings

Cocktail Bars

Tabac

  • What: Inventive cocktails, bartenders who’ll tailor drinks to your taste
  • Where: 10 Mitchell Lane, Glasgow G1 3NU (map)
  • Good for: Evening drinks, small groups, interesting conversation

The Alchemist

  • What: Theatrical cocktails and international food
  • Where: Unit 2, George House, George Square, Glasgow G2 1EH (map)
  • Good for: Pre-dinner drinks, spectacle, good veggie food too (see food page)

Live Music Venues with Good Bars

Mono

  • What: Vegan cafe/bar with record store and live music
  • Where: 12 Kings Court, King Street, Glasgow G1 5RB (map)
  • Good for: Indie/alternative music, vegan food, vinyl shopping (see food page)

The Hug and Pint

  • What: Vegan food upstairs, live music downstairs
  • Where: 171 Great Western Road, Glasgow G4 9AW (map)
  • Good for: Evening out combining food + music (see food page)

Quirky/Unique Bars

Tiki Bar & Kitsch Inn

  • What: Tropical-themed bar with massive rum selection and cocktails in tiki mugs
  • Where: 214 Bath Street, Glasgow G2 4HW (map)
  • Good for: Fun group outings, rum lovers, Instagram photos

Flight Club

  • What: Social darts venue with vintage fairground decor, bottomless pizza, and cocktails
  • Where: 32 North Frederick Street, Glasgow G1 2BS (map)
  • Good for: Groups, team bonding, something different

Whisky Bars

The Pot Still

  • What: Over 700 whiskies, a Glasgow institution since the 1880s
  • Where: 154 Hope Street, Glasgow G2 2TH (map)
  • Good for: Whisky lovers, real ale, traditional pub atmosphere

Late-Night Options

Many Glasgow pubs close at midnight on weeknights and 1am on weekends. For later options, Sauchiehall Street and Bath Street have the most late-night venues.

  • Relevance: Established community with engaged members who’d benefit from conference exposure.

Ladies of Code (Glasgow)

  • Website: https://www.meetup.com/ladies-of-code-glasgow/
  • About: Regular meetups celebrating and supporting women in the tech industry. Platform for networking, knowledge sharing, and collaboration.
  • Relevance: Active local group, likely receptive to a hackathon invite.

Coding Girls Glasgow

  • Website: https://glasgow.coding-girls.com/
  • About: Free coding events, workshops, and mentorship for girls and women in Glasgow.
  • Relevance: Ideal audience for beginner-friendly hackathon tasks.

Ada Scotland Festival

  • Website: https://ada.scot/
  • About: Focused on gender diversity in computing and tech in Scotland. Highlights the gap (19% female in Scottish Higher computing, 4.1:1 male:female ratio in UK computing degrees).
  • Relevance: Aligned mission; potential cross-promotion partner.

Code Division

  • Website: https://www.codedivision.co.uk/
  • About: Non-profit supporting underrepresented groups with digital skills. 83% of learners are women. Programmes in Cyber, Coding, Marketing, Data, and AI. 950+ learners upskilled.
  • Relevance: Their learners would gain real-world open source experience at the hackathon.

The Young Women’s Movement - Young Women Code

  • Website: https://www.youngwomenscot.org/young-women-code
  • About: Part of the broader Young Women’s Movement in Scotland. Addresses the 23% female representation in Scotland’s digital technology workforce.

Glasgow Women in Computing Science (GWiCS)

  • Website: https://www.gla.ac.uk/schools/computing/diversity/activities/
  • About: University of Glasgow group open to all staff and students (female/non-binary/male). Focus on research-level CS and above.
  • Relevance: University-based, could bring students and researchers.

item.title: Glasgow Restaurants Near the Venue
item.description:
Community over Code Glasgow 2026 - October 11-14, Hilton Glasgow

A guide to restaurants near the Community over Code Glasgow venue (Hilton Glasgow, 1 William St, city centre). The hotel sits right on the edge of Finnieston — Glasgow’s best dining strip — so you’re spoiled for choice within a 5–15 minute walk.

For vegetarian and vegan options specifically, see our dedicated Vegetarian & Vegan guide.

Fine Dining / Special Occasion

Cail Bruich ⭐

  • What: Michelin-starred modern Scottish. Seasonal, foraged, local. Chef Lorna McNee (Great British Menu judge).
  • Where: 725 Great Western Road, Glasgow G12 8QX (map)
  • Good for: The big team dinner. Book well in advance.

Unalome by Graeme Cheevers ⭐

  • What: Michelin-starred, elegant modern European in a period Finnieston building.
  • Where: 36 Kelvingrove Street, Glasgow G3 7RZ (map)
  • Good for: Special dinner, tasting menus. Very close to venue.

Scottish / Seafood

The Finnieston Bar & Restaurant

  • What: Award-winning seasonal Scottish seafood and craft cocktails. In a beautifully restored 1800s building.
  • Where: 1125 Argyle Street, Glasgow G3 8ND (map)
  • Good for: Fresh, sustainable seafood. Excellent gin selection.

Crabshakk

  • What: Small, beloved seafood spot — oysters, langoustines, whole crab, chowder.
  • Where: 1114 Argyle Street, Glasgow G3 8TD (map)
  • Good for: Informal seafood. No reservations for walk-ins — arrive early or queue.

Stravaigin

  • What: “Culinary adventure” — global flavours with local Scottish ingredients.
  • Where: 28 Gibson Street, Glasgow G12 8NX (map)
  • Good for: Inventive cooking, good veggie options, haggis done right.

Casual / Small Plates

Ox and Finch

  • What: Creative small plates, buzzy atmosphere. One of Glasgow’s best-loved restaurants for over a decade.
  • Where: 920 Sauchiehall Street, Glasgow G3 7TF (map)
  • Good for: Group dinners (sharing plates work well for big tables), cocktails.

Porter & Rye

  • What: Steak and cocktails. Dry-aged Scottish beef, craft drinks.
  • Where: 1131 Argyle Street, Glasgow G3 8ND (map)
  • Good for: Meat lovers. The rib-eye is the move.

Babbity Bowster

International

Cubatas

  • What: Valencian paella and classic tapas, run by Spanish chefs.
  • Where: 44 Queen Street, Glasgow G1 3DS (map)
  • Good for: Sharing plates, group-friendly, relaxed atmosphere.

Non Viet

  • What: Fresh Vietnamese — pho, spring rolls, curries, noodles. One of Glasgow’s first Vietnamese restaurants.
  • Where: 534 Sauchiehall Street, Glasgow G2 3LX (map)
  • Good for: Quick, vibrant, affordable. Also has a vegan offshoot in Partick.

Gloriosa

  • What: Italian — inventive pizzas and sharing plates. Focaccia sandwiches at lunch.
  • Where: 1321 Argyle Street, Glasgow G3 8AB (map)
  • Good for: Casual Italian, good for groups.

Chaophraya

  • What: Thai — largest Thai restaurant in Europe. Dedicated plant-based menu.
  • Where: 2 Nelson Mandela Place, Glasgow G1 2LL (map)
  • Good for: Big groups, great value set menus, strong veggie/vegan options.

Topolabamba

  • What: Mexican - small or large plates in a great atmosphere
  • Where: 89 St Vincent St, Glasgow G2 5TF (map)
  • Good for: Variety, sharing, good for groups

Chakoo Bombay Cafe

  • What: Indian & Persian - small plates
  • Where: 79 St Vincent St, Glasgow G2 5TF (map)
  • Good for: Groups, atmosphere

Quick / Budget

YO! Sushi

  • What: Conveyor-belt sushi, ramen, poke bowls.
  • Where: 79 George Street, Glasgow G1 1RD (map)
  • Good for: Fast, affordable, solo-friendly.

The Glasvegan

Quick Tips

  • Finnieston (Argyle Street between Kelvinhaugh St and Elderslie St) is Glasgow’s restaurant row — 5 min walk from the Hilton
  • Merchant City (east of George Square) is another cluster — 15 min walk or quick taxi
  • Booking: Popular spots fill up. Book ahead for groups of 6+.
  • Delivery: Deliveroo and Just Eat both cover the venue area well
  • Scottish things to try: Cullen skink (smoked haddock soup), haggis/neeps/tatties, Irn-Bru, tablet (Scottish fudge)

item.title: Glasgow Tourist Highlights
item.description:
Community over Code Glasgow 2026 - October 11-14, Hilton Glasgow

Attending Community over Code Glasgow? Here are the top things to see and do in Glasgow beyond the conference. Most are free and within easy reach of the venue.

Top Free Attractions

Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum

  • What: World-class art and natural history museum in a stunning red sandstone building. 22 galleries, everything from Dali to dinosaurs.
  • Where: Argyle Street, Glasgow G3 8AG (map)
  • Cost: Free
  • Time needed: 2-3 hours

Glasgow Cathedral

  • What: Medieval cathedral dating to the 12th century - one of the few Scottish medieval churches to survive the Reformation intact
  • Where: Castle Street, Glasgow G4 0QZ (map)
  • Cost: Free
  • Time needed: 45 min - 1 hour

Glasgow Necropolis

  • What: Atmospheric Victorian cemetery on a hill behind the Cathedral. 50,000+ burials, stunning city views, incredible monuments.
  • Where: Adjacent to Glasgow Cathedral (map)
  • Cost: Free
  • Time needed: 1 hour

Riverside Museum

  • What: Zaha Hadid-designed transport museum on the Clyde. Vintage cars, ships, locomotives, street scenes.
  • Where: 100 Pointhouse Road, Glasgow G3 8RS (map)
  • Cost: Free
  • Time needed: 2 hours

Gallery of Modern Art (GoMA)

  • What: Contemporary art in a neoclassical building. Look for the famous Duke of Wellington statue with a traffic cone on his head outside.
  • Where: Royal Exchange Square, Glasgow G1 3AH (map)
  • Cost: Free
  • Time needed: 1 hour

George Square

  • What: Glasgow’s principal city square, surrounded by grand Victorian architecture including City Chambers. As of October 2026 some parts of the square itself are closed.
  • Where: George Square, Glasgow G2 1DU (map)
  • Cost: Free
  • Time needed: 20 min to admire, or take the free City Chambers tour

The Glasvegan

Mono

Rose & Grants

  • What: Fully vegan cafe, open 7 days for breakfast and lunch
  • Where: 27 Trongate, Glasgow G1 5EZ (map)

Vegetarian-Friendly Restaurants (with extensive vegan options)

Chaophraya

The Alchemist

Ranjit’s Kitchen

  • What: Homemade Panjabi cuisine, very vegetarian-friendly
  • Where: 607 Pollokshaws Road, Glasgow G41 2QG (map)

The Prancing Stag

  • What: Award-winning neighbourhood restaurant (AA Rosette), seasonal Scottish food
  • Where: 1A Ashwood Gardens, Glasgow G13 1NX (map)
  • Good for: Special dinner with excellent veggie options (beside Jordanhill station)

Quick Tips

  • Many Glasgow restaurants label vegan options clearly on menus
  • “VG” = vegan, “V” = vegetarian on most Glasgow menus
  • Deliveroo and Just Eat both have strong vegan filters for Glasgow
  • The West End (Byres Road/Great Western Road area) has the highest concentration of veggie restaurants, accessible via Subway

item.title: Hackathon at Community over Code Glasgow 2026 — Retrospective
item.description:
We held a hackathon at Community over Code Glasgow 2026 (October 11–14, Hilton Glasgow). Projects brought real tasks and sat down together — new and experienced contributors alike — to work on them across the three days. This page is a retrospective of how it went. View the full poster.

What Happened

The hackathon ran throughout the conference (Monday through Wednesday) in the Wee Dram Room, with projects sharing the space across half-day slots. The room was busy every day, with a steady mix of focused project work and new people wandering in to find out how to get involved. Several project leads noted that the real value was as much in the face-to-face community time as in the code that got written — and that new contributors turned up as a direct result.
